volume: 第十二卷謬誤部 Volume 12: Errors and Fallacies Department

stories.text: 一人從京師回，自誇曾見皇帝。或問：「皇帝門景如何？」答曰：「四柱牌坊，金書『皇帝世家』。大門內匾，金書『天子第』。兩邊對聯是：『日月光天德，山河壯帝居。』」又問：「皇帝如何裝束？」曰：「頭帶玉紗帽，身穿金海青。」問者曰：「明明說謊，穿了金子打的海青，如何拜揖？」其人曰：「呸！你真是個冒失鬼，皇帝肯與那個作揖的？」
stories.translation: A man who had returned from the capital boasted that he had once seen the emperor. Someone asked, "What is the scenery at the emperor's gate like?" He replied, "Four-pillar archways with golden calligraphy reading 'Huangdi Shijia' (Imperial Family)." The plaque inside the main gate was inscribed in gold with "Tianzi Di" (Son of Heaven's Residence). The couplets on both sides read: "The sun and moon shine with the virtue of heaven; mountains and rivers magnify the imperial residence." Another asked, "How was the emperor dressed?" He said, "He wore a jade gauze hat on his head and a golden haiqing robe on his body." The questioner said, "You're clearly lying. If he wore a sea-blue robe made of gold, how could he bow and pay respects?" The man replied, "Hmph!" "You're really a careless fool. Would the emperor ever bow to anyone?"

stories.text: 一家父子僮僕，專說大話，每每以朝廷名色自呼。一日，友人來望，其父出外，遇其長子，曰：「父王駕出了。」問及令堂，次子又云：「娘娘在後花園飲宴。」友見說話僭分，含怒而去。途遇其父，乃述其子之言告之。父曰：「是誰說的？」僕在後云：「這是太子與庶子說的。」其友愈惱，扭僕便打。其父忙勸曰：「卿家弗惱，看寡人面上。」
stories.translation: A family of father, son, and servants always boasted recklessly, often referring to themselves by the names and titles of the imperial court. One day, a friend came to visit. The father was out and met his eldest son, who said, "His Majesty the King has gone out." When asked about your mother, the second son added, "The Empress is having a banquet in the back garden." The friend, seeing that their words were disrespectful and overstepped proper bounds, left in anger. On the way, he met the father and told him about his sons' remarks. The father asked, "Who said that?" A servant behind him said, "That was the Crown Prince and his younger son saying it." His friend became even more angry and turned to beat the servant. The father hurriedly tried to pacify him, saying, "Please don't be angry, for my sake as your Majesty."

stories.text: 有出外生理者，妻要捎買梳子，囑其帶回。夫問其狀，妻指新月示之。夫貨畢，忽憶妻語，因看月輪正滿，遂依樣買了鏡子一面帶歸。妻照之罵曰：「梳子不買，如何反取了一妾回來？」兩下爭鬧。母聞之往勸，忽見鏡，照云：「我兒有心費錢，如何討恁個年老婆兒？」互相埋怨，遂至訐訟。官差往拘之，差見鏡，慌云：「才得出牌，如何就出添差來捉違限？」及審，置鏡於案，官照見大怒云：「夫妻不和事，何必央請鄉官來講份上！」
stories.translation: A man who went out to conduct business was asked by his wife to buy a hair comb and bring it back. The husband asked what kind of comb she wanted, and the wife pointed at the crescent moon to show him. After finishing his business, the husband suddenly remembered his wife's words and looked up at the moon, which was full. So he bought a mirror in the shape of a full moon to bring back. The wife looked into it and scolded, "You didn't buy a comb; how come you brought home a concubine instead?" They quarreled loudly. Their mother heard about it and went to mediate, but when she saw the mirror, she looked into it and said, "My son wasted money with good intentions; how did he end up marrying such an old wife?" They blamed each other, which eventually led to a lawsuit. The officials sent by the court went to arrest them, and when they saw the mirror, one of the officers panicked and said, "We had just received our orders; how could we be caught violating the deadline so soon?" When they came to the trial, the mirror was placed on the table. The official looked into it and became furious, saying, "This is a matter of marital discord; why did you have to go as far as to involve local officials to plead your case!"

stories.text: 一官偶有書義未解，問吏曰：「此處有高才否？」吏誤認以為裁縫姓高也，應曰：「有。」即喚進，官問曰：「『貧而無諂』，如何？」答曰：「裙而無襉，折起來。」又問：「『富而無驕』，如何？」答曰：「褲若無腰，做上去。」官怒喝曰：「唗！」裁縫曰：「極是容易，若是皺了，小人有熨斗，取來燙湯。」
stories.translation: An official, who happened to have a passage in a book he could not understand, asked his clerk, "Is there any highly talented person here?" The clerk mistakenly thought the official was referring to a tailor surnamed Gao and replied, "Yes." He immediately called him in. The official asked, "What does 'poor but not fawning' mean?" The man answered, "A skirt without a hem—fold it up." He asked again, "What about 'rich but not arrogant'?" The answer was, "If pants have no waistband, just make them that way." The official angrily shouted, "Hmph!" The tailor said, "That's very easy. If it wrinkles, I have an iron; let me fetch some hot water to press it."

stories.text: 一官坐堂，偶撒一屁，自說「爽利」二字。眾吏不知，誤聽以為「賞吏」，冀得歡心，爭跪稟曰：「謝老爺賞。」
stories.translation: An official was sitting in court when he let out a fart and said the words "shuangli" (refreshing). The clerks did not understand and mistakenly heard it as "shangli" (reward the officials). Hoping to please him, they all knelt down in haste and said, "We thank you for your reward, sir."

stories.text: 有徽人開典而不識貨者，一人以單皮鼓一面來當，喝云：「皮鑼一面，當銀五分。」有以笙來當者，云：「斑竹酒壺一把，當銀三分。」有當笛者，云：「絲絹火筒一根，當銀一分。」後有持了事帕來當者，喝云：「虎狸斑漢巾一條，當銀二分。」小郎曰：「這物要他何用？」答云：「若還不贖，留他來抹抹嘴也好。」
stories.translation: There was a native of Hui who ran a pawnshop but did not know how to appraise goods. A man came in with a single-skin drum and the shopkeeper shouted, "One skin drum, worth five fen in silver." Another man came to pawn a sheng (a wind instrument), and the shopkeeper said, "A bamboo wine pot, worth three fen in silver." Someone came to pawn a flute, and he declared, "One silk fire tube, valued at one fen of silver." Later, someone came to pawn a handkerchief and the shopkeeper declared, "A tiger-spotted Han-style towel, worth two fen in silver." The young boy said, "What use is this thing?" He replied, "If it's not redeemed, at least we can keep it to wipe our mouths with."

stories.text: 有教小兒以「大」字者，次日寫「太」字問之，兒仍曰：「大字。」因教之曰：「中多一點，乃太公的太字也。」明日寫「犬」字問之，兒曰：「太公的太字。」師曰：「今番點在外，如何還是太字？」兒即應曰：「這樣說，便是外太公了。」
stories.translation: A man was teaching his son to write the character for "big" (大). The next day, when the boy wrote the character 太 and asked what it was, the child still said, "It's the 'big' character." The father then explained, "With an extra dot in the middle, it becomes the 'Tai Gong' (Grandfather) 太 character." The next day, when he wrote the 犬 character and asked him what it was, the boy said, "It's the 太 (Tai Gong) character." The teacher said, "This time the dot is outside; how can it still be the 'tai' character?" The boy immediately replied, "Then this means it's the grandfather from outside."

stories.text: 有賣床榻者，一日夫出，命婦守店。一人來買床，價少，銀水又低，爭值良久，勉強售之。次日，復來買榻，婦曰：「這人不知好歹，昨日床上討盡我便宜，今日榻上又想要討我的便宜了。」
stories.translation: There was a man who sold beds and couches. One day, when his husband went out, he ordered his wife to watch the shop. A man came in to buy a bed; the price was low and the silver content of his coins was also poor. They haggled for a long time before finally selling it reluctantly. The next day, the man came back to buy a couch. The woman said, "This man doesn't know good from bad; he took full advantage of me with the bed yesterday, and now he wants to take more advantage on the couch today."

stories.text: 一丈母命婿以房典銀，既成交，而房價未足。因作書促之云：「家岳母房事懸望至緊，刻不可緩，早晚望公垂慈一處，以濟其急。至感，至感。」
stories.translation: A mother-in-law ordered her son-in-law to pawn his house for silver. After the deal was made, however, the amount of silver received did not match the value of the property. She therefore wrote a letter urging him, saying: "My mother-in-law is anxiously waiting for the matter of the house; it cannot be delayed even for a moment. I hope you will kindly show your kindness and help her in this urgent need, day or night." "Deeply moved, deeply moved."

stories.text: 一家有糞一窖，招人貨賣，索錢一千，買者還五百。主人怒曰：「有如此賤糞，難道是狗撒的？」鄉人曰：「又不曾吃了你的，何須這等發急。」
stories.translation: A family had a cellar full of manure and invited people to buy it, asking for one thousand coins. A buyer offered five hundred in return. The owner angrily said, "If the manure is so cheap, could it possibly be from a dog?" A local person replied, "It's not like we've eaten your manure; why are you getting so worked up about it?"

stories.text: 有屠牛者，過宰豬者之家，其子欲諱「宰豬」二字，回云：「家尊出亥去了。」屠牛者歸，對子述之，稱贊不已。子亦領悟，次日屠豬至，其子亦回云：「家父往外出丑去了。」問：「幾時歸？」答曰：「出盡丑醜仝自然回來了。」
stories.translation: There was a butcher who passed by the house of another pig slaughterer. The son wanted to avoid using the words "zai zhu" (to slaughter pigs) and replied, "My father has gone out for the hour Hai." When the cattle butcher returned home, he told his son about it and praised him repeatedly. The son also understood the idea; on the next day when he went to slaughter a pig, his son replied, "My father has gone out to be shamed." Asked, "When will he return?" Answered, "He'll naturally come back once all the shame is done."

stories.text: 一嫂前行而裙夾於臀縫內者，叔從後拽整之。嫂顧見，疑其調戲也，遂大怒。叔躬身曰：「嫂嫂請息怒，待愚叔依舊與你塞進去，你再夾緊何如？」
stories.translation: A sister-in-law was walking ahead with her skirt caught in the crotch. Her brother-in-law, following behind, pulled it out and fixed it for her. The sister-in-law looked back and saw this; suspecting that he was making a pass at her, she became very angry. The brother-in-law bowed and said, "Dear sister-in-law, please calm down. Let me, your humble younger uncle, put it back in for you as before; how about you then hold it tight again?"

stories.text: 兄患病獻神，嫂收祭物，叔將嫂臂暗掐一把。嫂怒云：「看你肥肉吃得幾塊！」兄在床上聽見，叫聲：「兄弟沒正經，你嫂嫂要留來結識人頭的，大家省口出客罷。」
stories.translation: The elder brother was ill and offerings were made to the gods. The sister-in-law collected the sacrificial items, when her younger brother-in-law secretly pinched her arm. The sister-in-law angrily said, "Just see how many pieces of fatty meat you've eaten!" The elder brother, lying in bed and hearing this, called out, "Brother, you're not behaving properly. My sister-in-law is to be kept for future introductions; let's all save our words and avoid entertaining guests."

stories.text: 一人不通文墨，向友問曰：「三點水的『淫』字如何解？」友曰：「淫乃婦人之大病。」其人頷之。一日，此人之妻忽抱病頗劇，出遇友人問曰：「令正病體何如？」其人曰：「不要說起，賤內這兩日，著實一發淫得緊哩。」
stories.translation: A man, who was illiterate, asked a friend, "How do you explain the character 'yin' (lust) with three water radicals?" The friend said, "Lust is a great illness for women." The man nodded in agreement. One day, this man's wife suddenly fell seriously ill. When he met a friend and was asked, "How is your wife's illness?" The man said, "Don't even mention it. My poor wife has been getting really lustful these two days."

stories.text: 一人元旦出門云：「頭一日必得利市方妙。」遂於桌上寫一「吉」字。不意連走數家，求一茶不得。將「吉」字倒看良久，曰：「原來寫了『口干』二字，自然沒得吃了。」再順看曰：「吾論來，竟該有十一家替我潤口。」
stories.translation: A man went out on New Year's Day saying, "It is essential to gain profit or good fortune on the first day." So he wrote a "Ji" (auspicious) character on the table. Unluckily, after visiting several households, he could not even get a cup of tea. After staring at the "Ji" character upside down for a long time, he said, "Ah, I see now. I actually wrote the words 'kou gan' (dry mouth), so of course no one gave me anything to eat." Looking at it right side up again, he said, "According to my calculation, there should have been eleven households that would have given me something to moisten my mouth."

stories.text: 一生好健訟。一日，妻在坑廁上撒尿，見月色照在妻腚，乃大怒，遂以月照妻腚事，訟之于官。縣令不解其意，掛牌拘審。生以實情訴稟，求父師伸冤。官怒曰：「月照你妻的腚就來告理，倘日晒你妻的屄，你待要怎麼？」
stories.translation: A man had a habit of frequently initiating lawsuits. One day, while his wife was urinating at the latrine, he saw moonlight shining on her buttocks and became very angry. He then took the matter to court over the issue of moonlight illuminating his wife's buttocks. The county magistrate did not understand the case and ordered him to be detained for interrogation. The man explained the actual situation, pleading with his father-teacher (a respectful term for a scholar or teacher) to clear his name. The official angrily said, "You come to file a lawsuit because the moonlight shines on your wife's buttocks? If the sun were to shine on her private parts, what would you do then?"

stories.text: 有兄弟經商，學得一二官話。將到家，兄往隔河出恭，命弟先往見其父。父問曰：「汝兄何在？」弟曰：「撒屎。」父驚曰：「在何處殺死的？」答曰：「河南。」父方悲慟而兄已至，父遂罵其次子：「何得妄言如是？」曰：「我自打官話耳。」父曰：「這樣官話，只好嚇你親爺罷了。」
stories.translation: There were brothers who engaged in business and learned a little of the official language. As they were about to arrive home, the older brother went across the river to relieve himself and ordered his younger brother to go first and see their father. The father asked, "Where is your elder brother?" The younger brother replied, "Defecating." The father was startled and asked, "Where has he been killed?" He replied, "In Henan." Just as the father was grieving, the older brother arrived. The father then scolded his second son, saying, "How could you speak so falsely?" The younger brother said, "I was just speaking official language." The father said, "Such official language is only good for scaring your own grandfather."

stories.text: 一鄉人進城，偶與人競，被打耳光子數下。赴縣叫喊，官問：「何事？」曰：「小人被人打了許多乳光。」官不信，連問，只以乳光對。官大怒，呼皂隸掌嘴。方被掌，鄉人遽以指示官，正是這個樣子。
stories.translation: A villager went into the city and, by chance, got into a competition with someone else. He was slapped several times across the face. He went to the county office to complain loudly. The official asked, "What happened?" The man replied, "I was hit by many ranguang." The official did not believe him and asked repeatedly. The villager only answered with the word "ranguang." The official became very angry, called for a bailiff, and ordered that he be slapped in the face. Just as he was being slapped, the villager quickly showed it to the official, saying this is exactly what happened.

stories.text: 一鄉人涉訟，官受其賄，臨審復掌嘴數下。鄉人不忿，作官話曰：「老牙，你要人觜我就人觜，要銅團就銅團，要尾就尾，為何臨了來又歹我的乳廣？」
stories.translation: A villager got involved in a lawsuit. The official, having accepted his bribe, slapped him several times across the face during the trial. The villager was not satisfied and said in official language, "Old man, if you want my lips, I'll give you my lips; if you want copper balls, here are the copper balls; if you want the tail, here is the tail. Why did you slap me again at the end?"

stories.text: 一大氣脬過關，關吏見之，指其夾帶漏稅。其人辯曰：「小的是疝氣病。」吏曰：「既是扇子柄，難道不要起稅的麼？」曰：「疼的疝氣病。」吏曰：「藤扎扇子柄，一發要報稅了。」其人曰：「老爺，不是，是疼的大氣脬。」吏怒曰：「銅的大剃刀，豈該容汝漏稅？責打二十，以正其罪！」此人被打出來，偶為尿急，對人家門首撒之。門內婦人大罵，其人曰：「娘子休罵，我這官物，比眾不同，才在衙門裡納過稅，娘子就請看何妨。」
stories.translation: A man with a large balloon passed through the customs. The customs officer saw it and pointed out that he was smuggling and evading taxes. The man defended himself, saying, "It's a hernia." The officer said, "If it is the handle of a fan, would you not have to pay tax on it?" He replied, "It's a painful hernia." The officer said, "If it is a fan handle tied with vines, you would have to report and pay the tax for it immediately." The man said, "Sir, no, it's a large balloon that hurts." The officer angrily said, "A copper big shaving razor—shouldn't you have to pay taxes on it?" "He was beaten twenty times to correct his crime!" After being beaten and driven out, the man happened to feel an urgent need to urinate. He then relieved himself in front of someone's door. The woman inside the house scolded him fiercely. The man said, "Madam, please don't shout. This is official property; it's different from ordinary things. It has just been taxed at the courthouse. Madam may take a look if you wish."

stories.text: 一人初上北路，才騎牲口踏鐙，掉落一鞋。其人因作官話大聲曰：「阿呀，掌鞭的，我的鞋。」趕鞭的以為喚他做爺，答云：「爺不敢。」其人愈發急，大呼曰：「我的鞋，我的鞋！」掌鞭的不會其意，亦連聲回應曰：「爺，小的怎麼敢？」其人只得仍作鄉語，怒罵曰：「搠殺那娘，我一隻鞋子脫掉了！」
stories.translation: A man was just starting his journey north. As he mounted a beast of burden and stepped onto the stirrup, one of his shoes fell off. The man then loudly said in official language: "Oh no! The whip holder, my shoe!" The whip holder thought he was being called 'master' and replied, "I dare not." The man became even more anxious and shouted, "My shoe! My shoe!" Still not understanding the meaning, the whip holder also responded repeatedly, saying, "Master, how dare I?" The man had no choice but to switch back to his local dialect and angrily cursed, "Damn it! I dropped one of my shoes!"

stories.text: 一杭人婦，催轎往西湖遊玩，貪戀湖上風景，不覺歸遲。時已將暮，怕關城門，心中著急，乃對轎夫言曰：「轎夫阿哥，天色晚了，我多把銀錢打發，你與我盡力鬧一鬧。早行進到裡頭去，不但是我好，連你們也落得自在快活些。」
stories.translation: A woman from Hangzhou urged the sedan chair to take her for a tour of West Lake. She became so enamored with the scenery that she returned home late without realizing it. As evening was approaching, she feared the city gates would close and became anxious. She then said to the sedan chair bearer, "Brother sedan chair man, it is getting late. I will give you extra silver money; please do your best to make a scene." "Get inside as soon as possible. Not only will I be fine, but you all will also have a more comfortable and pleasant time."

stories.text: 婦人門首買菜，問：「幾個錢一把？」賣者說：「實價三個錢兩把。」婦還兩個錢三把，賣者云：「不指望我來摸娘娘一把，娘娘倒想要摸我一把，討我這樣便宜。」
stories.translation: A woman was buying vegetables at the gate and asked, "How much for one bundle?" The seller said, "The actual price is three coins for two bundles." The woman countered, "Two coins for three bundles," and the seller said, "I didn't expect you to give me a feel, but instead you want to take advantage of me by getting such a good deal."

stories.text: 一人初往蘇州，或教之曰：「吳人慣扯空頭，若去買貨，他討二兩，只好還一兩。就是與人講話，他說兩句，也只好聽一句。」其人至蘇，先以買貨之法，行之果驗。後遇一人，問其姓，答曰：「姓陸。」其人曰：「定是三老官了。」又問：「住房幾間？」曰：「五間。」其人曰：「原來是兩間一披。」又問：「宅上還有何人？」曰：「只房下一個。」其人背曰：「原還是與人合的。」
stories.translation: A man was going to Suzhou for the first time. Someone advised him, "People from Wu are used to giving empty promises. If you go to buy goods and they ask for two taels, you should only offer one tael." "Even when talking with people, if they say two sentences, you should just listen to one of them." When the man arrived in Suzhou, he first applied this method when buying goods and found it effective. Later, he met a person who asked his surname. The man replied, "I am surnamed Lu." The man said, "You must be Sanlaoguan (a respectful term)." He then asked, "How many rooms do you have in your house?" The man replied, "Five." The other person said, "Originally it is two rooms with one attached room." He then asked, "Who else lives in your house?" The man replied, "Only one person under the roof." The other person remarked behind his back, "It turns out he still lives with others."

stories.text: 吳人有灌園者，被鄰居竊去蔬果，乃大罵曰：「入娘賊，春天偷了我嬸（筍），夏天又來偷我妹（梅）子，到冬來還要偷我個老婆（蘿卜）。」
stories.translation: A man from Wu who tended a vegetable garden was robbed of his vegetables and fruits by his neighbor. He angrily cursed, "You damned thief! In spring you stole my shen (bamboo shoots), in summer you stole my meizi (plums), and now in winter you even want to steal my laopo (wife) (radish)."

stories.text: 蘇州人家晒晾兩榪桶在外，瞽者不知，誤撒小解。其姑喝罵，嫂忙問曰：「這肏娘賊個膿血，滴來你個裡面，還是撒來我個裡頭。」姑回云：「我搭你兩邊都有點個。」
stories.translation: A family in Suzhou had two buckets for drying things outside. A blind man, unaware of them, mistakenly urinated there. His grandmother scolded him fiercely, and his sister-in-law quickly asked, "This damned thief—did the urine drip into yours or did he urinate in mine?" The grandmother replied, "There's a bit of it on both sides."

stories.text: 一家養子瞞人，鄰翁問其婦曰：「娘子恭喜，添了令郎。」婦曰：「並無此事，要便是你鳥出來的。」
stories.translation: A family had a child in secret. A neighborly old man asked the woman, "Madam, congratulations on having another son." The woman said, "There is no such thing; if there must be one, it's the bird that came out of yours."

stories.text: 姑嫂二人地上軋棉花，嫂問姑：「軋得幾何？」姑曰：「盡力軋得兩腿酸麻，軋個戎（毧）勿出。」
stories.translation: An grandmother and her daughter-in-law were carding cotton on the ground. The daughter-in-law asked the grandmother, "How much have you carded?" The grandmother replied, "I worked so hard that my legs became sore and numb, but I still couldn't card out a single tuft of cotton."

stories.text: 松江有嫗誕辰，子侄輩商所以慶生者。一曰：「叫伙戲子與渠湯湯，好弗熱鬧。」一曰：「個非阿娘所好，弗如尋幾個和尚，與渠篤篤倒好。」
stories.translation: In Songjiang, there was an old woman whose birthday had arrived. Her sons and nephews discussed what to do for her birthday celebration. One suggested, "Let's hire some actors to perform a play for her; it will be lively and festive." Another said, "That is not what Mother likes. It would be better to find a few monks and have them chant for her."

stories.text: 賀友壽者，其友先期躲生，鎖門而出。一日，路上遇見，此人慣作歇後語，因對友曰：「前兄壽日，弟拉了許多喪門吊客，替你生災作賀，誰料你家入地無門，竟是披枷帶（鎖）了。」
stories.translation: A guest who came to celebrate his friend's birthday found that the friend had left early, locking the door behind him. One day, when they met on the road, this man was in the habit of using proverbs and said to his friend, "On your birthday, I brought many mourners as guests to celebrate with you. Who knew that your house had no entrance, so all we did was bring shackles (locked doors) for you."

stories.text: 一老翁壽誕，親友醵分，設宴公祝，正行令，各人要帶說「壽」字。而壺中酒忽竭，主人大怒，客曰：「為何動壽氣（器）？」一客云：「欠檢點，該罰。」少頃，又一人唱壽曲，傍一人曰：「合差了壽板。」合席皆曰：「一發該罰。」
stories.translation: An old man celebrated his birthday. Relatives and friends pooled their money to hold a banquet in his honor. During the drinking game, everyone had to include the word "shou" (longevity) in their remarks. Suddenly, the wine in the pot ran out, and the host became very angry. A guest asked, "Why did you touch the longevity qi (vessel)?" One guest said, "You were careless; you should be punished." A little while later, another person sang a longevity song. A man beside him said, "You missed the beat of the shou board." Everyone at the table said, "He should be punished as well."

stories.text: 眾客飲酒，要譬字《四書》一句為令，說不出者，罰一巨觥。首令曰：「譬如為山。」次曰「譬如行遠必自邇」，以及「譬之宮牆」等句。落後一人無可說得，乃曰：「能近取譬。」眾嘩然曰：「不如式該罰。如何譬字說在下面？」其人曰：「屁原該在下，諸兄都從上來，不說自倒出了，反來罰我？」
stories.translation: Several guests were drinking alcohol, and they set a rule: whoever could not come up with an analogy from the Four Books would be punished by drinking a large cup of wine. The first guest said, "For example, building a mountain." Next came "for instance, walking far must start from nearby," and other lines such as "like the palace wall." The last person could not think of anything else to say, so he said, "Take a nearby example." Everyone laughed and said, "That doesn't fit the rule; you should be punished." "How can an analogy word appear at the end?" The person said, "Originally, 'pi' (fart) should be at the bottom. All of you gentlemen came from above; you didn't even say anything and it just naturally came out. Why are you punishing me?"

stories.text: 飲酒行令，座客有茫然者。一友戲曰：「不知令，無以為君子也。」其人詰曰：「不知命，為何改作令字？」答曰：「《中庸》注云：『命猶令也。』」
stories.translation: While drinking and playing a game with rules, one guest at the table looked completely clueless. A friend joked, "If you don't know the rule, you cannot be considered a gentleman." The person retorted, "Why did you change 'ming' (fate) to 'ling' (rule)?" He replied, "The commentary on the Zhongyong says: 'Ming is similar to ling.'"

stories.text: 夫妻二人對飲，妻勸夫行令。夫曰：「無色盆奈何？」妻指腰間曰：「色盆在此，要你行色令，非行酒令也。」夫曰：「可。」遂解褲出具就之，但苦其物之不硬。妻大叫曰：「令官不舉，該罰一杯。」
stories.translation: A husband and wife were drinking together, and the wife urged her husband to play a game with rules. The husband said, "What if there is no colored basin?" The wife pointed to her waist and said, "The 'colored' basin is right here. I want you to play the 'color' game, not a drinking game." The husband said, "Okay." He then unzipped his pants and presented it to her, but he was troubled by the fact that it wasn't hard. The wife shouted, "Since the official in charge of the rule isn't performing, you should be punished with a cup of wine."

stories.text: 鄉人夤緣進學，與父兄叔伯暑天同走，惟新生撐傘。人問何故，答曰：「入學不晒（十惡不赦）。」
stories.translation: A fellow townsman used connections to gain admission into the school. During a summer outing with his father, elder brothers, and uncles, only the new student carried an umbrella. When people asked why, he replied, "Not getting sun exposure after enrollment is considered one of the ten unpardonable crimes."

stories.text: 蘇州人有賣餛飩者，夫偶出，令其妻守店，姿色甚美。一人來買餛飩，因貪看想慕出神，叫曰：「娘子，我要買你飩（臀）。」婦應曰：「你為何脫落子餛（魂）囉？」
stories.translation: In Suzhou, there was a man who sold wontons. One day his husband happened to be out and asked his wife to watch the shop; she was very beautiful in appearance. A man came to buy wontons, and he was so captivated by her beauty that he stared at her absentmindedly. He called out, "Madam, I want to buy your 'dumplings' (buttecks)." The woman replied, "Why did you drop your soul ('hun')?"

stories.text: 一婦人向山客買茶葉，客問曰：「娘子還是要細的，要粗的？」婦曰：「粗細倒也都用得著，只不要屑（泄）。」
stories.translation: A woman was buying tea leaves from a mountain dweller. The seller asked, "Madam, would you like the fine or the coarse ones?" The woman said, "Both fine and coarse are useful, just don't want any shavings (leaks)."

stories.text: 一糖擔歇在人家門首敲鑼，婦喝曰：「快請出去，只管在此挲甚麼？挲出個小的兒來，又要害我淘氣。」
stories.translation: A candy seller stopped at the entrance of a house and rang a bell. A woman shouted, "Go away quickly! Why are you just standing here making noise?" "Ringing that bell will bring out some little child and cause me more trouble."

stories.text: 一家請客，擺列水果。家主母取甘蔗食之，連聲叫淡。廚司曰：「娘娘想是梢（騷）了。」
stories.translation: A family was hosting a banquet, and they had arranged various fruits. The host's mother took some sugar cane to eat but kept calling it bland. The cook said, "Madam, perhaps you are just feeling a bit restless (sao)."

stories.text: 天赦日秤人，婆先將媳上秤，婆云：「娘子，你放在大花星上正好。」次秤婆，媳云：「看婆婆不出，到（倒）梢（騷）了。」
stories.translation: On the day of general amnesty, when people were being weighed, the grandmother-in-law first put her daughter-in-law on the scale and said, "Madam, you are just right for the big flower star." Next, when weighing herself, the daughter-in-law said, "I can't see you clearly; it seems like you are getting a bit out of hand (sao)."

stories.text: 兩人相遇，各問所生子女幾何。一曰：「五女。」一曰：「一子。」生女者曰：「一子是險子。」生子者怒曰：「我是蜆子，強如你養了許多肉蚌。」
stories.translation: Two people met and asked each other how many children they had. One said, "Five daughters." The other replied, "One son." The one with daughters said, "A single son is a risky thing (xianzi)." The one who had a son angrily replied, "I am an oyster, better than you raising so many soft-shelled clams."

stories.title_en: Steamed Buns Coming Out of the Steamer
stories.text: 一女人暑天賣饅頭，一人進店取一個，拍開一聞，以其葷者，仍合攏不買而去。店主母大罵曰：「掰開屄個天殺的！我家這樣初出籠的饅頭，香噴噴，粉白肥嫩，不差甚麼，你也用得過。為甚走進來拍開一條大縫，嗅了一嗅，竟自去了。」
stories.translation: A woman was selling steamed buns on a hot summer day. A man entered the shop, took one bun, patted it open to smell it, and since he found it smelly, closed it again without buying and left. The shop owner's mother scolded loudly, "You opened my bun, you damned son of a bitch!" "These buns from our home just out of the steamer are fragrant, white, soft, and tender. They're not lacking anything at all, yet you still had to touch them." "Why did you come in, tear a big gap open, sniff it for a moment, and then just leave?"

stories.text: 一女買綿子，正在講價，賣者欲出小恭，躊躇不決。女云：「你放在此，難道我偷了不成？」其人曰：「既如此，大娘綿（眠）在凳上，待我撒出了來。」
stories.translation: A woman was buying cotton, and while they were haggling over the price, the seller wanted to take a small break but hesitated. The woman said, "You can leave it here; would I steal from you?" The man replied, "If that's the case, Auntie, just lie (mian) on the stool and wait for me to finish."

stories.text: 一人問鄰婦借秤，婦回云：「我家這管撒屁秤，是用不得的。」其人曰：「娘子，你在前另有不撒屁的，求借我用一用。」
stories.translation: A man asked his neighbor's wife to borrow a scale, and she replied, "The fart scale in my house is not usable." He said, "Madam, don't you have another one that doesn't fart? I would like to borrow it for a while."

stories.text: 一貓向婦人求食，叫喚不止。婦喝曰：「只管叫甚麼，除非割下這張屄來與你吃。」鄰漢聽得曰：「娘子，你若當真，我就去買碎魚來換。」
stories.translation: A cat begged from a woman for food and kept meowing nonstop. The woman scolded, "Just keep on yowling like that! Unless you cut off this thing and give it to you to eat." A neighbor heard her and said, "Madam, if you're serious, I'll go buy some ground-up fish to trade for it."

stories.text: 一人夜膳後，先在板凳上去睡，翻身說：「底下硬得緊。」妻在灶前聽見，回言曰：「不要忙，收拾過碗盞就來了。」
stories.translation: After a night meal, one man lay down on a bench first and turned over, saying, "It's very hard underneath." His wife, who was at the stove, heard this and replied, "Don't worry; I'll come after I finish cleaning up the bowls and chopsticks."

stories.text: 一人年逾四旬始議婚，自慚太晚，飾言續弦。及娶後，妻察其動靜，似為未曾婚者。乃問其前妻何氏，夫驟然不及思，遽答曰：「手氏。」
stories.translation: A man, who had only started to discuss marriage after the age of forty, felt ashamed it was too late and pretended to say he was going to remarry. After getting married, his wife observed his behavior and realized that he seemed like a man who had never been married before. She then asked about the surname of his previous wife, and without thinking, he hastily replied, "The Hand Clan."

stories.text: 丈夫欲娶妾，妻曰：「一夫配一婦耳，娶妾見於何典？」夫曰：「孟子云：『齊人有一妻一妾。』又曰：『妾婦之道。』妾自古有之矣。」妻曰：「若這等說，我亦當再招一夫。」夫曰：「何故？」妻曰：「豈不聞《大學》上云：『河南程氏兩夫』。《孟子》中亦有『大丈夫』、『小丈夫』。」
stories.translation: The husband wanted to take a concubine, and his wife said, "One man is matched with one woman. Where in the classics does it say anything about taking a concubine?" The husband replied, "Mencius said: 'A man from Qi had one wife and one concubine.'" He added, "'The way of the concubine and wife.'" "Therefore, concubines have existed since ancient times." The wife said, "If that's how it is, I should also take another husband." The husband asked, "Why?" The wife replied, "Haven't you heard in the Great Learning that it says: 'Cheng Shi of Henan had two husbands.'" "There is also mention of 'great husband' and 'small husband' in the Mencius."

stories.text: 中秋出賣月餅，招牌上錯寫日餅。一人指曰：「月字寫成白字了。」其人曰：「我倒信你騙，白字還有一撇哩！」
stories.translation: On Mid-Autumn Festival, mooncakes were being sold, but the sign mistakenly read "sun cakes." A person pointed and said, "The character for 'moon' was written as a 'white' character instead." The shopkeeper replied, "I don't believe you're trying to trick me; the character for 'white' still has a stroke!"

stories.text: 牆腳下恐人撒尿，畫一烏龜於壁上，且批其後曰：「撒尿者即是此物。」一人不知那裡，仍去屙溺。其人罵曰：「瞎了眼睛，也不看看。」撒尿者曰：「不知老爹在此。」
stories.translation: To prevent people from urinating at the base of a wall, someone painted a turtle on the wall and wrote behind it: "Anyone who urinates here will become this creature." A man didn't know where to go and still went to urinate there. The person scolded, "Are your eyes blind? Don't you look around?" The urinator replied, "I didn't know you were here, old man."

stories.text: 牆上畫一烏龜，專禁人屙尿。一人竟撒，主家喝曰：「你看！」其人云：「原來烏龜在此看我撒尿。」
stories.translation: A turtle was painted on the wall to specifically prohibit people from urinating there. One man still went ahead and urinated, and the homeowner shouted, "Look!" The man said, "So this turtle is here watching me urinate."

stories.text: 主人謂僕曰：「汝出外，須說幾句大話，裝我體面。」僕領之。值有言「三清殿大」者，僕曰：「只與我家租房一般。」有言「龍衣船大」者，曰：「只與我家帳船一般。」有言「牯牛腹大」者，曰：「只與我家主人肚皮一般。」
stories.translation: The master told his servant, "When you go out, you must say a few big things to enhance my reputation." The servant accepted the order. When someone mentioned that "the Three Purity Hall is very large," the servant said, "It's only as big as my master's rented house." When someone mentioned that "the dragon robe ship is large," he said, "It's only as big as our family's boat." When someone mentioned that "the ox's belly is large," he said, "It's only as big as the master of our house's stomach."

stories.text: 兩人好大言。一人唇說：「敝鄉有一大人，頭頂天，腳踏地。」一人曰：「敝鄉有一人更大，上嘴唇觸天，下嘴唇著地。」其人問曰：「他身子藏在那裡？」答曰：「我只見他掙得一張大口。」
stories.translation: Two people loved to make big claims. One man boasted, "In my hometown, there is a great person whose head touches the sky and feet touch the earth." Another said, "There is an even bigger man in my hometown, whose upper lip touches the sky and lower lip touches the ground." The first person asked, "Where is his body hidden?" He replied, "I only saw him stretching one big mouth."

stories.text: 一人說：「昨日某處，天上跌下一個人來，長十丈，大二丈。」或問之曰：「亦能說話否？」答曰：「也講幾句。」曰：「講甚麼話？」曰：「講天話。」
stories.translation: One person said, "Yesterday at a certain place, a man fell down from the sky. He was ten zhang tall and two zhang wide." Someone asked him, "Could he speak as well?" He replied, "Yes, he spoke a few sentences." They asked, "What kind of words did he speak?" He said, "He spoke heavenly talk."

stories.text: 一說謊者曰：「敝處某寺中有一鼓，大幾十圍，聲聞百里。」傍又一人曰：「敝地有一牛，頭在江南，尾在江北，足重有萬餘斤，豈不是奇事？」眾人不信。其人曰：「若沒有這隻大牛，如何得這張大皮，慢得這面大鼓？」
stories.translation: A liar said, "In a certain temple of our place, there is a drum that is dozens of circles in circumference and its sound can be heard for hundreds of li." Another person beside him said, "In my area there is a cow whose head is in Jiangnan and tail in Jiangbei. Its weight alone exceeds ten thousand jin—wouldn't that be an extraordinary thing?" The crowd did not believe it. That person said, "If there were no such big cow, how could we get this large hide to make this big drum?"

stories.text: 好說謊者對人曰：「敝處某寺有一腳盆，可使千萬人同浴。」聞者不信。傍一人曰：「此是常事，何足為奇？敝地一新聞，說來才覺詫異。」人問：「何事？」曰：「某寺有一竹林，不及三年，遂長有幾百萬丈，如今頂著天公長不上去，又從天上長下來。豈不是奇事？」眾人皆謂誑言。其人曰：「若沒有這等長竹，叫他把甚麼篾子，箍他那隻大腳盆？」
stories.translation: A habitual liar said to others, "There is a foot basin in a certain temple of our town that can allow thousands of people to bathe together." Those who heard this did not believe it. A person beside them said, "This is a common thing; what's so strange about it?" "In our area there was a news story that, when spoken of, truly seems astonishing." Someone asked, "What happened?" He said, "In a certain temple there is a bamboo forest that, within less than three years, grew hundreds of thousands of zhang. Now it has grown up to the heavens and cannot grow any higher, so it continues growing downward from the sky." Wouldn't that be a strange thing?" Everyone considered it to be false talk. The man said, "If there were not such long bamboo, what kind of bamboo strips would they use to bind that big foot basin?"

stories.text: 山東人慕南方大橋，不辭遠道來看。中途遇一蘇州人，亦聞山東蘿蔔最大，前往觀之。兩人各訴企慕之意。蘇人曰：「既如此，弟只消備述與兄聽，何必遠道跋涉？」因言：「去年六月初三，一人自橋上失足墮河，至今年六月初三，還未曾到水，你說高也不高？」山東人曰：「多承指教。足下要看敝處蘿蔔，也不消去得，明年此時，自然長過你們蘇州來了。」
stories.translation: A man from Shandong admired the large bridges in the south and traveled a long distance to see them. On his way, he met a man from Suzhou who had also heard that the radishes in Shandong were the largest and was going to see them. The two men each explained their longing and admiration. The Suzhou man said, "If that is the case, I can just describe it to you, Brother; there's no need for a long and arduous journey." He then said, "Last year on the third day of the sixth lunar month, a person fell into the river from the bridge by accident. As of today, the third day of the sixth moon this year, he has still not reached the water. Do you think it is high or not?" The man from Shandong said, "I am greatly indebted for your instruction. "If you want to see our radishes, there's no need to go at all; by this time next year, they will naturally grow over to your Suzhou."

stories.text: 一人過橋，貼邊而走，傍人謂曰：「看仔細，不要踏了空。」其人誤聽說他偷了葱，因而大怒，爭辨不已。復轉訴一人，其人曰：「你們又來好笑，我素不相認，怎麼冤我盜了鐘？」互相廝打，三人扭結到官。官問三人情事，拍案恚曰：「朝廷設立衙門，叫我南面坐，爾等反叫我朝了東！」制簽就打。官民爭鬧，驚動後堂。適奶奶在屏後竊聽，聞之柳眉倒豎，搶出堂來，拍案吵鬧曰：「我不曾幹下歹事，為何通同眾百姓要我嫁老公！」
stories.translation: A man was crossing a bridge and walked close to the edge. A passerby told him, "Be careful not to step into empty space." The man misheard it as saying he had stolen scallions and became very angry, arguing endlessly. He then turned to complain to another person, who said, "You two are being ridiculous again. I have never known you before; how could you falsely accuse me of stealing a bell?" They fought each other and the three men were taken to court in a tangle. The official asked about the situation of the three men and slammed his desk in anger, saying, "The imperial court established this office to have me sit facing south. You dare turn my back east instead!" He ordered them to be beaten immediately. The commotion between the official and the people alarmed the back hall. At that moment, the grandmother was eavesdropping behind a screen. Upon hearing this, she raised her eyebrows in anger and rushed out to the hall, slamming the desk while shouting, "I have not done anything wrong; why are you all conspiring with the common people to make me marry an old husband!"

stories.text: 松江人無子，一友問：「尊嫂曾養否？」其人答曰：「房下養（同癢）是常常養呢，只是孽（入看）深招（抓看）勿得。」
stories.translation: A man from Songjiang had no children. A friend asked, "Has your wife ever given birth?" The man replied, "We often have intimacy, but it's just that the place is too deep to reach."

stories.text: 松江婦寒天淘米，似手冷插入腰內。主母疑其偷米，喝曰：「做甚麼？」婦答云：「手木（摸）篤（音屄，手冷也）。」
stories.translation: A woman from Songjiang was washing rice on a cold day and seemed to insert her cold hands into her waist. The mistress suspected she had stolen the rice and shouted, "What are you doing?" The woman replied, "My hands were cold (shǒu mō dǔ, meaning 'cold hands')."

stories.text: 有人慣會說謊，其僕每代為圓之，一日，對人說：「我家一井，昨被大風吹往隔壁人家去了。」眾以為從古所無，僕圓之曰：「確有其事。我家的井，貼近鄰家籬笆，昨晚風大，把籬笆吹過井這邊來，卻像井吹在鄰家去了。」一日，又對人說：「有人射下二雁，頭上頂碗粉湯。」眾又驚詫之，僕圓曰：「此事亦有。我主人在天井內吃粉湯，忽有一雁墮下，雁頭正跌在碗內，豈不是雁頭頂著粉湯。」一日，又對人說：「寒家有頂漫天帳，把天地遮得沿沿的，一些空隙也沒有。」僕乃攢眉曰：「主人脫煞扯這漫天謊，叫我如何遮掩得來。」
stories.translation: There was someone who often lied, and his servant always helped cover it up. One day, he said to others, "A well in my house was blown by the strong wind into a neighbor's yard yesterday." The crowd thought it was something unprecedented. The servant covered for him, saying, "It really happened. Our family's well is close to the neighbor's fence. Last night, when the wind was strong, it blew the fence over toward our well, making it seem as if the well had been blown into their yard." One day, he said to people again, "Someone shot down two geese with a bowl of congee on their heads." The crowd was surprised once more. The servant explained, "This also happened. My master was eating congee in the courtyard when suddenly a goose fell down. The goose's head landed right into the bowl, so isn't that like the goose had congee on its head?" One day, he again told people, "My home has a canopy that covers the entire sky and completely blocks out the heavens and earth, leaving not even a single gap." The servant frowned and said, "My master is telling an outrageous lie. How can I possibly cover it up?"
